# Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags — facts

## Structure and components

- [statement] `UpdateOne` changes at most one matching document and requires a nonempty update document containing update operators. `ReplaceOne` replaces at most one matching document and its replacement must not contain update operators. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/blob/master/mongo/collection.go · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/how-to-use-mongodb-with-go/

## How it works

- [statement] Setting `UseJSONStructTags` enables fallback to a `json` tag when a `bson` tag is absent. The documented client configuration applies BSON options through `SetBSONOptions`. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/blob/master/mongo/options/clientoptions.go · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/current/data-formats/bson.md, https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/bson
- [statement] A BSON struct tag specifies a BSON field name and optional comma-separated options. The bson:"restaurant_id,omitempty" tag renames RestaurantId and omits it when empty. (medium confidence) — https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/bson · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/current/data-formats/struct-tagging.md
- [statement] minsize stores supported integer fields as BSON int32 when their values fit, otherwise retaining BSON int64. truncate permits fractional BSON doubles to be truncated when decoding into non-float numeric fields. (medium confidence) — https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/bson · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/current/data-formats/bson.md

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Avoid duplicate field names in bson.D: the BSON API documentation warns that duplicate key names can cause undefined server behavior. (low confidence) — https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/bson · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A nil `bson.D` used as a sort document can trigger a `WriteNull` error in CRUD marshaling. The driver troubleshooting guide distinguishes `var sort bson.D` from an initialized empty `bson.D{}`. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/blob/master/docs/common-issues.md · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags

## Facts and statements

- [statement] `bson.M` does not provide stable field order: the driver serializes its elements in undefined order, consistent with the Go language specification leaving map iteration order unspecified. (high confidence) — https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/bson · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://go.dev/ref/spec, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/blob/master/bson/primitive.go
- [statement] Only exported struct fields participate in default BSON marshaling and unmarshaling. Default keys lowercase Go field names; BSON struct tags override the stored field name. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/current/data-formats/bson.md · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/current/data-formats/struct-tagging.md, https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/bson
- [statement] `InsertOne` accepts a struct document and applies its BSON tags during insertion; the struct-tag example inserts a `Restaurant` with a custom `restaurant_id` key and omits empty tagged fields. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/current/data-formats/struct-tagging.md · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/blob/master/mongo/collection.go, https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/how-to-use-mongodb-with-go/
- [statement] `DeleteOne` removes at most one matching document. A successful no-match delete reports `DeletedCount` equal to `0`; a successful no-match `UpdateOne` reports `MatchedCount` equal to `0`. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/blob/master/mongo/collection.go · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/how-to-use-mongodb-with-go/
- [statement] omitempty omits zero-valued numbers, booleans and strings, zero-length slices, maps and arrays, and nil pointers or interfaces. By default a struct is empty only if it implements Zeroer and IsZero returns true; ordinary structs are not automatically omitted. (low confidence) — https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/bson · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags
- [statement] The `inline` BSON tag flattens a struct or map field into its containing BSON document and reverses that flattening during unmarshaling. Untagged embedded struct fields instead become subdocuments. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/current/data-formats/bson.md · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/bson
- [statement] Scope unordered-filter advice carefully: equality against an entire embedded document requires an exact match including field order. A Go user thread illustrates intermittent misses with nested `bson.M`, whereas ordered `bson.D` preserves the equality document order. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-embedded-documents.md · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/75253113/mongodb-golang-findone-with-nested-bson-m-failed-for-10-attempts-bson-mbso, https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/bson
- [statement] The community discussion distinguishes field order inside a BSON document from element order in an outer slice: `[]bson.M` preserves slice element order while each map remains unordered. For multiple sort fields, the discussion recommends `bson.D` to preserve sort precedence. (medium confidence) — https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66272948/is-order-of-array-of-bson-m-maintained-in-mongodb-go-driver · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/64281675/bson-d-vs-bson-m-for-find-queries
- [statement] A nil pointer marshals as BSON null; a non-nil pointer marshals as its underlying type. (medium confidence) — https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/bson · keywords: Go driver CRUD, bson.D versus bson.M and struct tags · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/current/data-formats/bson.md
